## Narrative

The metabolite panel is dominated by **arachidonic acid (C00219) metabolism**. RaMP enrichment returned a cluster of six matching compounds — arachidonic acid, 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717), and 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid (C14768) — across multiple highly enriched SMPDB pathways (FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment ≥ 633). All of these top-ranked hits map explicitly to **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (SMP00075)**, a central inflammatory lipid cascade. The two remaining metabolites, 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid (C01161) and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156), resolve to separate KEGG pathways (Ubiquinone Biosynthesis; Phenylalanine metabolism) and do not contribute to the arachidonic acid cluster, suggesting they represent independent oxidative or xenobiotic signatures in this dataset.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid is the obligatory upstream precursor. KEGG BFS confirms it is reachable *in two enzymatic steps* to leukotriene A4 (via C05356, an unstable hydroperoxide intermediate) and to 5-HETE (also via C05356), validating the directionality of the cascade. Leukotriene A4 is a highly reactive epoxide intermediate; its detection alongside its downstream HETE products is consistent with a treatment that stabilises or shunts the lipoxygenase branch of the pathway. 15-HETE and 5-HETE are lipoxygenase-derived hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids whose elevation signals enhanced 12/15-LOX and 5-LOX activity, respectively. 15-Deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 is a cyclopentenone prostaglandin with recognised electrophilic reactivity toward NF-κB and PPARγ, placing it at the intersection of inflammatory signalling and metabolic regulation.

**Biological significance.** Co-enrichment of the 5-LOX branch (leukotriene A4, 5-HETE) with the 12/15-LOX branch (15-HETE) and the epoxyeicosatrienoic acid (EET) analogue (5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid) indicates broad activation of all three major arachidonic acid oxidative pathways — lipoxygenase, cytochrome P450, and cyclooxygenase — consistent with an acute inflammatory stimulus, oxidative stress, or pharmacological intervention (e.g., NSAID/aspirin exposure, as reflected in the parallel drug-action pathway enrichment). The presence of 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 further suggests PPARγ-mediated anti-inflammatory gene regulation is co-activated. Changes in the two phenolic acids may reflect secondary modulation of mitochondrial coenzyme Q biosynthesis or phenylalanine catabolism, processes known to be sensitive to oxidative tone. The combined lipid signature points to a robust, system-wide re-programming of arachidonic acid flux through multiple enzymatic arms.

## Narrative

The eight metabolites fall into two distinct clusters based on RaMP enrichment. Six compounds — arachidonic acid (C00219), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717), and 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid (C14768) — co-enrich in **Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency (SMP00353)** with FDR = 0.0 and fold-enrichment = 643.3, and appear together across seven additional high-scoring drug-action pathways including **Acetylsalicylic Acid Action Pathway (SMP00083)**, **Salicylate-sodium Action Pathway (SMP00708)**, and **Acetaminophen Action Pathway (SMP00710)**. The remaining two metabolites, 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid (C01161) and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156), are not members of this arachidonic acid cluster.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid is the upstream precursor of the six-cluster metabolites. KEGG BFS confirms arachidonic acid is reachable in two enzymatic steps to leukotriene A4 (via C05356, a hydroperoxide intermediate) and to 5-HETE (also via C05356), validating the directionality of the cascade. Leukotriene A4 is a reactive epoxide intermediate; its detection alongside downstream HETE products is consistent with altered flux through the lipoxygenase arm of the pathway. 15-HETE and 5-HETE are hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids whose elevation indicates enhanced lipoxygenase activity. 15-Deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 is a cyclopentenone prostaglandin that is also a member of the Arachidonic Acid Metabolism pathway (SMP00075 / KEGG map00590) and appears in the same drug-action enrichment results, suggesting it is part of the same arachidonic acid–derived cascade.

**Biological significance.** The six-compound cluster is strongly associated with drug-action pathways involving NSAIDs and salicylates (FDR = 0.0), consistent with a treatment that perturbs arachidonic acid metabolism. The presence of leukotriene A4 alongside 5-HETE and 15-HETE points to concurrent activation of the lipoxygenase branch. 3,4-Dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid is linked by RaMP to tyrosine metabolism and neuronal system pathways, indicating an independent signal not shared with the arachidonic acid cluster.

**Limitations.** The two phenolic acids (3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) are not co-enriched with the arachidonic acid cluster in this dataset, and direct upstream/downstream relationships between them and the eicosanoid panel could not be verified from the available KEGG graph data.
